title: Billing Operations Standard: Allocation of Banked Credit Across Aggregated Service Agreements (Net Energy Metering)
content:
**Standard.** Under a Net Energy Metering rider that allows aggregation, banked credit offsets the offsettable charges of the generating service agreement first, and then of the other aggregated service agreements of the same customer, up to the rider's maximum number of aggregated agreements, in the order of the rider's allocation basis, each up to the offsettable charges of its bill for the same billing period. Agreements of another customer, agreements outside the rider's contiguity rule and closed agreements never receive credit. Under every other rider credit offsets only the generating service agreement.

## Terms used in this standard

- **Offsettable charges of a bill**: the bill's energy charge plus its Power Supply Cost Recovery charge, less any Net Energy Metering credit already applied against that bill.
- **Aggregated service agreements**: the customer's other service agreements, in active or notice pending status on the handling date, that meet the rider's contiguity rule. The rider's figures (whether aggregation is allowed, the maximum number of agreements, the contiguity rule and the allocation order) are those of the rider's credit offset and aggregation terms.

## Who may receive credit

| Service agreement | Receives credit under an aggregating rider |
|---|---|
| The generating service agreement | Yes, first |
| Another agreement of the same customer, active or notice pending, within the contiguity rule, within the maximum number | Yes, in allocation order |
| An agreement of another customer | Never |
| An agreement outside the contiguity rule | Never |
| A closed agreement | Never |

## Hypothetical worked allocation

Hypothetical inputs: an aggregating rider whose order is the generating agreement first and then the others oldest start date first; a bank of 900.00; offsettable charges for the same billing period of 420.00 on the generating agreement, 310.00 on an aggregated agreement started earlier and 260.00 on one started later.

- The generating agreement is offset by 420.00, leaving 480.00.
- The earlier-started agreement is offset by 310.00, leaving 170.00.
- The later-started agreement is offset by 170.00, the rest of the bank; 90.00 of its offsettable charges remain to be paid.

Under a rider that does not allow aggregation, the same bank offsets only the generating agreement's 420.00.

title: Settlement Worksheet — Anniversary Cash-Out and Retained Credit (Net Energy Metering)
content:
This worksheet fixes the anniversary cash-out of a Net Energy Metering agreement and the credit retained in its bank.

**Anniversary cash-out.** The credit bank balance recorded on the agreement less the retained credit, rounded to the cent and never below zero.

**Retained credit.** The retention months multiplied by the average monthly applied credit, plus the fixed retention, plus the paired battery capacity in kWh multiplied by the storage retention rate, plus the number of bills of the hosting service agreement dated in the 12 months before the cash-out that were issued on an estimated closing read multiplied by the estimate buffer, the sum rounded to the cent once.

## Values used

| Element | Value |
|---|---|
| Average monthly applied credit | The credit applied on the most recent bill, from the net metering history |
| Retention months | None |
| Fixed retention | None |
| Storage retention rate | None |
| Estimate buffer | None |
| Paired battery capacity | As recorded on the agreement |
| Estimated bills counted | Bills of the hosting service agreement dated in the 12 months before the cash-out issued on an estimated closing read |

## Order of the calculation

1. Each of the four parts of the retained credit is formed: the retention months multiplied by the average monthly applied credit; the fixed retention; the paired battery kWh multiplied by the storage retention rate; the number of estimated bills multiplied by the estimate buffer.
2. The four parts are added and the total is rounded to the cent once.
3. The retained credit is deducted from the credit bank balance; a negative result is taken as zero, and the cash-out is rounded to the cent.

## Hypothetical worked figure

Hypothetical inputs: a credit bank balance of 486.25, a paired battery of 13.5 kWh, credit of 41.80 applied on the most recent bill, and two estimated bills in the 12 months.

- Retained credit: none of the four parts adds anything, so 0.00.
- Anniversary cash-out: 486.25 less 0.00, that is 486.25, and the bank stands at 0.00 afterwards.

title: Anniversary True-Up Cash-Out — Net Energy Metering Settlement Rule
content:
**Scope.** Under Net Energy Metering, this rule governs the anniversary cash-out booked at the bill dated in the true-up month of an operating agreement under a rider whose true-up disposition is cash out.

**Disposition at the anniversary.** At the anniversary true-up of a rider whose true-up disposition is cash out, the anniversary cash-out is paid by check and the retained credit stays in the bank and opens the new true-up year. A rider whose true-up disposition is carry forward leaves its residual bank in the bank at the anniversary, and a rider whose true-up disposition is forfeit forfeits it.

**When the cash-out is fixed.** The anniversary cash-out is fixed only after the bank carries the expiry entry owed for credit carried into the closing true-up year and left unused by its bills. Until the bank carries that expiry entry, the anniversary cash-out is not fixed.

**Method of payment.** A cash-out of at least the rider's check minimum is paid by check.

## Disposition by rider at the anniversary

| True-up disposition | Riders | At the bill dated in the true-up month |
|---|---|---|
| Cash out | Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering, Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering, Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff, Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff | Anniversary cash-out paid by check; retained credit stays in the bank and opens the new true-up year |
| Carry forward | Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff | Residual bank stays in the bank |
| Forfeit | Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering | Residual bank forfeited |

After the cash-out the net metering history shows an anniversary payout paid by check, and the agreement's credit bank balance is the credit that remains.

## Paying the cash-out — `settle_anniversary_cash_out_8d85c400`

**Capability.** The tool records, dated the day it is run, one anniversary payout entry paid by check in the agreement's net metering history for the stated amount, and lowers the agreement's banked credit by that amount; whatever credit remains stays banked.

**How it is invoked.** It is a representative's tool: the representative unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `nem_agreement_id` | Reference number of the net metering agreement (interconnection application number), read from the net metering agreement lookup | Identifier |
| `payout_usd` | Anniversary cash-out paid by check | USD, positive decimal with 2 decimal places, rounded to the cent |

**Return.** On success the receipt carries `status` "paid"; `nem_ledger_id`, the reference number of the payout entry; `nem_agreement_id`; `settlement_date`, the day's date in YYYY-MM-DD; `payout_method` "check"; `amount`, the payout in USD with 2 decimals; and `credit_bank_balance`, the agreement's banked credit in USD with 2 decimals after the payout.

title: Interconnection Handbook — Eligibility of Net Energy Metering Applications and the System Size Cap
content:
## Conditions of acceptance

An application under Net Energy Metering is accepted only when every one of the following holds:

1. **Rider open.** The rider applied for is open to new applications, and the customer and the service agreement meet the rider's customer class and entry requirements.
2. **Active service agreement.** The service agreement whose premises host the system is in active status in the company's records at the time the application is taken.
3. **Capacity range.** The system capacity lies between the rider's smallest and largest system size, in kW AC.
4. **Size cap.** The system capacity multiplied by the rider's expected annual output per kW may not exceed the rider's size cap fraction multiplied by the annual usage of the address.
5. **Battery.** A paired battery is accepted only where the rider allows storage, and only up to the rider's largest paired battery capacity.
6. **Meter.** The service agreement may not hold a Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter in service, because net metering requires a bidirectional communicating meter; a customer who wants net metering must first return to a communicating meter.

**Design facts.** The system capacity, the generator type and the battery capacity are taken from the customer's installer design as the customer states them.

**Legacy rider.** Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering accepts no new applications; an existing legacy agreement keeps its terms for the rider's grandfathering years after permission to operate, unless the rule on modifications that lose grandfathering applies to it.

## Annual usage of the address

The annual usage is the total metered kWh of the most recent regular bills of the service agreement before the application date, as many bills as the rider's look-back; where fewer bills exist, the customer's stated annual load estimate is used.

## Source of each fact

| Fact | Where it is taken from |
|---|---|
| Status of the service agreement | Company records, read before the application is taken |
| Annual usage | The service agreement's bills, or the customer's stated load estimate where the bills are fewer than the look-back |
| System capacity, generator type, battery capacity | The customer's statement of the installer design |
| Meter in service | Company metering records |

## Size cap at the boundary (hypothetical)

Hypothetical inputs: a rider with expected output of 1150 kWh per kW and a cap fraction of 1.10, and an address with 10450 kWh of annual usage. The cap is 11495 kWh.

| System capacity | Expected output | Within the cap |
|---|---|---|
| 9.9 kW AC | 11385 kWh | Yes |
| 9.995 kW AC | 11494.25 kWh | Yes |
| 10.0 kW AC | 11500 kWh | No |

Expected output equal to the cap is within it; only output above the cap fails.

title: Net Energy Metering Interconnection Application Fee
content:
**Charge.** Each Net Energy Metering application is charged the rider's fixed application fee plus the rider's additional fee per kW AC multiplied by the system capacity, the total rounded to the cent, on the application date. The fee is charged once per application and is not refunded on rejection, withdrawal or expiry. A modification within the modification limit carries no application fee.

The fixed fee and the per-kW fee are the figures of the rider's interconnection application terms.

## The charge broken down

| Element | Value |
|---|---|
| Amount | The fixed application fee, plus the per-kW fee multiplied by the nameplate capacity in kW AC |
| Rounding | Once, to the cent, on the total |
| Date | The application date |
| Frequency | Once per application; the company's records of the application show whether the fee has already been charged |
| Refund | None on rejection, withdrawal or expiry |
| Modification within the limit | No fee |

## Worked figures

- Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff, 30.0 kW AC system: 145.00 plus 1.00 multiplied by 30.0, that is 175.00.
- Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering, 12.5 kW AC system: 800.00 plus 2.00 multiplied by 12.5, that is 825.00.
- Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff, 157.25 kW AC system: 1500.00 plus 2.00 multiplied by 157.25, that is 1814.50.
- Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering, any size: 75.00, since the per-kW fee is 0.00.

## Basis questions

**An application is withdrawn before approval. Is the fee returned?** No. The fee is not refunded on rejection, withdrawal or expiry.

**A customer applies again after an approval expired. Is a fee charged?** Yes. Each application is charged its own fee once.

title: Billing Operations Rule — Averaging Applied Credit for the Net Energy Metering Anniversary Cash-Out
content:
The average monthly applied credit used in the Net Energy Metering anniversary cash-out is averaged over a full year or over the last quarter, depending on how many regular bills the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system has had in the year and how many of its bills were estimated.

**Rule.** When the hosting service agreement has at least the full-year bill count of 12 regular bills dated in the 12 months before the cash-out and at most one bill dated in those months issued on an estimated closing read, the average monthly applied credit is the credit applied for billing periods ended in those 12 months divided by 12, rounded to the cent. When it has at least 12 regular bills and two or more estimated bills, it is the credit applied for billing periods ended in the 3 months before the cash-out divided by 3, rounded to the cent. With fewer than 12 regular bills in the 12 months, neither average is taken.

**Records read.** The bill kind, read type and bill date of each bill of the hosting Electric Service Agreement; the credit applications in the net metering history and the billing periods they belong to.

## Averaging method

| Regular bills dated in the 12 months | Bills dated in the 12 months issued on an estimated read | Average monthly applied credit |
|---|---|---|
| 12 or more | 0 or 1 | Credit applied for billing periods ended in the 12 months, divided by 12, rounded to the cent |
| 12 or more | 2 or more | Credit applied for billing periods ended in the 3 months, divided by 3, rounded to the cent |
| Fewer than 12 | Any | Neither average is taken |

## Hypothetical worked cases

- Twelve regular bills, one of them estimated, and credit applied of 538.20 for the year's billing periods: 538.20 divided by 12 is 44.85.
- Twelve regular bills, two estimated, and credit applied of 151.30 for the last 3 months' billing periods: 151.30 divided by 3 is 50.4333, so 50.43.

title: Settlement Desk Rule: Average Monthly Offsettable Charges at a Net Energy Metering Move-Out
content:
At a Net Energy Metering move-out termination the average monthly offsettable charges are taken from the bills of the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system, according to that agreement's status and whether it has a final bill.

**Rule.** When the hosting service agreement is closed and has a final bill, the average monthly offsettable charges are the energy charges plus the Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of its regular bills dated in the 12 months before the termination, divided by the number of those regular bills, rounded to the cent. When the hosting service agreement is active and has no final bill, they are the same sums over all of its bills dated in those 12 months, divided by their number, rounded to the cent. In any other case this twelve-month averaging does not apply.

**Records read.** The status of the hosting Electric Service Agreement (active, closed, and so on), whether a final bill has been issued on it, and for each of its bills the bill date, the bill kind (regular or final), the energy charge and the Power Supply Cost Recovery charge.

## Method by status

| Hosting service agreement | Bills averaged | Divided by |
|---|---|---|
| Closed, with a final bill | Regular bills dated in the 12 months before the termination (the final bill is left out) | The number of those regular bills |
| Active, with no final bill | All bills dated in the 12 months before the termination | The number of those bills |
| Any other status or combination | Twelve-month averaging does not apply | — |

## Hypothetical worked case

Hypothetical inputs: a closed hosting service agreement with a final bill and 11 regular bills dated in the 12 months before the termination, whose energy charges total 858.66 and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges total 24.31.

- Sum of the charges: 882.97.
- Average: 882.97 divided by 11, that is 80.27.

title: Paired Battery Retention Rate at the Net Energy Metering Anniversary Cash-Out
content:
When a battery is paired with a Net Energy Metering system, credit is retained in the bank at the anniversary cash-out at a rate per kWh of paired battery capacity, and the rate depends on whether the customer holds an active enrollment in Demand Response Programs.

**Rule.** When a battery is paired with the system and the customer holds an active demand response enrollment, the storage retention rate is the dispatch storage rate of 0.50 USD per kWh. When a battery is paired and the customer holds no active demand response enrollment, it is the other storage rate of 1.50 USD per kWh. Without a paired battery no storage retention rate applies.

**Records read.** The paired battery capacity in kWh recorded on the net metering agreement (0 when none); the status of the customer's Demand Response Programs enrollments, of which at least one must be active for the dispatch rate.

## Storage retention rate

| Paired battery | Active Demand Response Programs enrollment | Rate (USD per kWh of battery capacity) |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | 0.50 |
| Yes | No | 1.50 |
| No | Any | None |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A 13.5 kWh battery, customer with an active enrollment: 0.50 per kWh.
- The same battery, customer whose only enrollment has been removed: 1.50 per kWh.
- No battery recorded on the agreement: no rate.

title: Net Energy Metering Credit Offset and Aggregation Terms by Rider
content:
Banked Net Energy Metering credit offsets only certain charges on a bill, carries from bill to bill within the true-up period, and under one rider may be shared with the customer's other service agreements. The rider terms are:

## Charges the credit may offset and carryover

| Rider | Charges banked credit may offset | Unused credit carries to the next bill within the true-up period |
|---|---|---|
| Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering | Energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges; never the customer charge or fees | Yes |
| Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering | Energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges; never the customer charge or fees | Yes |
| Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff | Energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges; never the customer charge or fees | Yes |
| Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff | Energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges; never the customer charge, demand charge or fees | Yes |
| Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering | Energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges; never the customer charge, demand charge or fees | Yes |
| Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff | Energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges; never the customer charge, demand charge or fees | Yes |

## Aggregation

| Rider | Aggregation allowed | Most additional service agreements aggregated | Which service agreements may be aggregated | How credit is shared |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering | Yes | 10 | Service agreements of the same customer on the generating parcel or on parcels contiguous or adjacent to it | The generating agreement first, then the other aggregated agreements in order of their start date, oldest first, each up to its offsettable charges |
| Rider NEM-L, Rider NEM-R, Rider NBT-R, Rider NBT-C and Rider NBT-L | No | 0 | Not applicable | Not applicable |

## Points of the terms

- Only Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering allows aggregation; the other five riders show 0 additional agreements.
- Up to 10 additional service agreements may share the credit under Rider NEM-A, besides the generating agreement.
- Hypothetical illustration: under Rider NEM-A, a generating agreement and two aggregated agreements started in 2016 and 2019 receive credit in the order generating agreement, the 2016 agreement, then the 2019 agreement.

title: Tariff Interpretation Note: Order in Which Net Billing Bills Draw on Carried Credit (Net Energy Metering)
content:
Under the Net Energy Metering riders valued at the avoided-cost export rates — Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff, Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff and Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff — the share of a closing true-up year's applied credit that came out of carried credit depends on whether the rate schedule of the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system has on-peak hours.

**Rule.** When the schedule of the hosting service agreement has on-peak hours and the rider values exports at the avoided-cost export rates, the year's bills draw on that year's own export credits first, and the carried credit used is the credit applied in excess of the year's export credits, or zero when there is no excess. When the schedule has no on-peak hours and the rider values exports at the avoided-cost export rates, the carried credit used is the year's applied credit multiplied by the carried credit divided by the sum of the carried credit and the year's export credits, rounded to the cent. Under a retail-valued rider neither of these drawing orders applies.

**Terms.** The year's export credits and the year's applied credit are those of the billing periods of the closing true-up year in the net metering history; the carried credit is the credit carried into that year.

## Drawing order

| Rider | Hosting schedule | Carried credit used |
|---|---|---|
| Avoided-cost rider | Has on-peak hours | Applied credit in excess of the year's export credits; zero when there is no excess |
| Avoided-cost rider | No on-peak hours (flat) | Applied credit in proportion to the carried credit's part of carried credit and year's export credits together, rounded to the cent |
| Retail-valued rider | Any | Neither drawing order applies |

## Hypothetical worked cases

Hypothetical inputs: carried credit 340.00, year's export credits 420.00, year's applied credit 470.00.

- Time-of-use schedule: the year's export credits are drawn first; 470.00 less 420.00 leaves 50.00 drawn from carried credit.
- Flat schedule: 470.00 multiplied by 340.00 divided by 760.00 is 210.263, so 210.26 drawn from carried credit.
- Time-of-use schedule with applied credit of 400.00: no excess over 420.00, so zero.

title: Settlement Desk Rule — Expiry of Carried Net Energy Metering Credit at the Anniversary True-Up
content:
**Scope.** Under Net Energy Metering, this rule governs the expiry of carried credit at the anniversary true-up booked at the bill dated in the true-up month.

**Rule.** At each anniversary true-up of a rider whose true-up disposition is cash out or carry forward, credit carried into the closing true-up year and left unused by its bills expires and is booked as an anniversary forfeiture of the expired carried credit. Under a rider whose true-up disposition is forfeit, the residual bank is still forfeited in full at each anniversary true-up, and no carried credit arises.

## Riders and the anniversary expiry

| Rider | True-up disposition | Expiry of carried credit at the anniversary |
|---|---|---|
| Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering | Cash out | Applies |
| Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering | Cash out | Applies |
| Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff | Carry forward | Applies |
| Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff | Cash out | Applies |
| Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff | Cash out | Applies |
| Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering | Forfeit | No carried credit arises; the residual bank is forfeited in full |

**Effect in the records.** The expiry appears in the net metering history as an anniversary forfeiture entry for the expired carried credit, dated the day it is booked, and the agreement's credit bank balance falls by that amount.

## Booking the expiry — `expire_carried_credit_d622768b`

**Capability.** The tool records, dated the day it is run, one anniversary forfeiture entry in the agreement's net metering history for the stated amount of carried credit that has expired, and lowers the agreement's banked credit by that amount. Afterwards the history shows the forfeiture with settlement kind anniversary.

**How it is invoked.** It is a representative's tool: the representative unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `nem_agreement_id` | Reference number of the net metering agreement (interconnection application number), read from the net metering agreement lookup | Identifier |
| `expired_credit_usd` | Dollar amount of carried credit that expires | USD, positive decimal with 2 decimal places, rounded to the cent |

**Return.** On success the receipt carries `status` "expired"; `nem_ledger_id`, the reference number of the forfeiture entry; `nem_agreement_id`; `settlement_date`, the day's date in YYYY-MM-DD; `amount`, the expired credit in USD with 2 decimals; and `credit_bank_balance`, the agreement's banked credit in USD with 2 decimals after the entry.

title: Applying Banked Net Energy Metering Credit to Bills
content:
**Rule.** On each bill of an operating Net Energy Metering agreement, banked credit is applied up to the offsettable charges of that bill, including the export credit banked for the same billing period. Credit never offsets the customer charge, demand charges, fees, program debits or past-due balances, and any unused bank carries to the next bill where the rider provides monthly carryover. Each bill is offset once.

**Amount applied.** The credit applied to a bill is the lesser of the credit bank balance and the bill's offsettable charges.

**Offsettable charges.** The bill's energy charge plus its Power Supply Cost Recovery charge, less any Net Energy Metering credit already applied against that bill.

## Charges on a bill

| Charge | Offset by banked credit |
|---|---|
| Energy charge | Yes |
| Power Supply Cost Recovery charge | Yes |
| Customer charge | Never |
| Demand charge | Never |
| Fees | Never |
| Program debits | Never |
| Past-due balances | Never |

## Once per bill

Whether a bill has already been offset is read from the company's net metering history for that bill; a bill already carrying a credit application is not offset again.

## Hypothetical illustrations

| Bank before the bill (including the same period's export credit) | Offsettable charges | Credit applied | Bank carried to the next bill |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64.20 | 88.75 | 64.20 | 0.00 |
| 150.00 | 88.75 | 88.75 | 61.25 |
| 88.75 | 88.75 | 88.75 | 0.00 |

In each case the customer charge, any demand charge and any fees on the bill remain payable in full.

title: Seasonal Daylight Factor for Estimated Net Energy Metering Exports
content:
An estimated Net Energy Metering export credit is scaled for the change in daylight when the estimated period and the preceding period fall in different pricing seasons on the bills of the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system.

**Rule.** When the preceding period's bill is a summer bill and the estimated period's bill is a winter bill, the daylight factor is the summer-to-winter factor of 0.72. When the preceding period's bill is a winter bill and the estimated period's bill is a summer bill, the daylight factor is the winter-to-summer factor of 1.30. When both bills carry the same season, no daylight adjustment applies.

**Bills compared.** The estimated period's bill is the most recent service bill of the hosting Electric Service Agreement. The preceding period's bill is the service bill whose billing period ends on the billing period end of the most recent export credit in the net metering history. The season of each is the pricing season printed on it.

## Daylight factor by season pair

| Preceding period's bill | Estimated period's bill | Daylight factor |
|---|---|---|
| Summer | Winter | 0.72 |
| Winter | Summer | 1.30 |
| Summer | Summer | No daylight adjustment |
| Winter | Winter | No daylight adjustment |

## Hypothetical illustration

Hypothetical inputs: an estimate basis of 450 kWh. Following a summer bill into a winter bill, the basis is scaled by 0.72; following a winter bill into a summer bill, by 1.30; between two winter bills, it is not scaled for daylight.

title: Schedule of Charges — Early Exit Charge on Ending a Net Energy Metering Agreement
content:
An early exit charge is deducted from the bank when a customer ends a Net Energy Metering agreement before the rider's export rate lock period has run.

**Rule.** When the whole calendar months from the permission to operate date to the termination are fewer than the rider's export rate lock years multiplied by 12 and a battery is paired with the system, the early exit charge is the system's nameplate capacity in kW AC multiplied by the per-kW early exit rate of 2.50, rounded to the cent. When those months are fewer than that and no battery is paired, it is the flat early exit charge of 75.00. Otherwise no early exit charge applies.

**Records read.** The permission to operate date, the nameplate capacity in kW AC and the paired battery capacity recorded on the agreement; the rider's export rate lock years.

## Lock period by rider

| Rider | Export rate lock years | Months below which the charge applies |
|---|---|---|
| Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering | 0 | 0 (no month count is below it, so no charge) |
| Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering | 0 | 0 (no charge) |
| Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff | 9 | 108 |
| Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff | 9 | 108 |
| Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering | 0 | 0 (no charge) |
| Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff | 9 | 108 |

## Charge

| Whole months from permission to operate to the termination | Battery paired | Early exit charge |
|---|---|---|
| Fewer than the lock months | Yes | Nameplate kW AC multiplied by 2.50, rounded to the cent |
| Fewer than the lock months | No | 75.00 |
| Equal to or more than the lock months | Any | None |

## Hypothetical worked cases

- Rider NBT-R, 7.6 kW AC system with a 13.5 kWh battery, 40 months after permission to operate: 7.6 multiplied by 2.50, a charge of 19.00.
- The same system without a battery: 75.00.
- Rider NBT-C system terminated 107 months after permission to operate: charge applies; at 108 months: none.

title: Customer Care Academy — Estimate Buffer at the Net Energy Metering Anniversary Cash-Out
content:
At the anniversary cash-out of a Net Energy Metering agreement, a buffer is retained for each bill of the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system that was issued on an estimated closing read during the year.

**Rule.** When at least one bill dated in the 12 months before the cash-out was issued on an estimated closing read and the most recent bill was itself issued on an estimated closing read, the estimate buffer is the estimated-close buffer of 40.00 per estimated bill. When at least one such bill exists and the most recent bill was not issued on an estimated closing read, it is the actual-close buffer of 20.00 per estimated bill. With no estimated bill in the 12 months, no estimate buffer applies.

## Questions and answers

**Which bills are looked at?** The bills of the hosting Electric Service Agreement dated in the 12 months before the cash-out, with their read types, and the most recent bill of that agreement.

**Three bills of the year were estimated, the latest one among them. What is the buffer?** 40.00 per estimated bill, because the most recent bill was itself estimated.

**Three bills of the year were estimated, but the most recent bill was an actual read. What is the buffer?** 20.00 per estimated bill.

**No bill of the year was estimated. Is a buffer retained?** No estimate buffer applies.

## Buffer per estimated bill

| Estimated bills in the 12 months | Most recent bill | Buffer per estimated bill (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| One or more | Estimated | 40.00 |
| One or more | Actual or customer read | 20.00 |
| None | Any | None |

title: Estimation Worksheet — Amount of an Estimated Net Energy Metering Export Credit
content:
This worksheet fixes the export kWh, the rates and the amount of the export credit banked under Net Energy Metering for a billing period closed on an estimated read.

## Inputs

- **Preceding export credit**: the most recent export credit in the net metering history, the one with the latest billing period end. Its recorded on-peak and off-peak export kWh together make the preceding period's total export kWh; its recorded on-peak and off-peak rates are the rates used.
- **Estimate basis**: the preceding period's total export kWh, carried over unscaled.
- **Daylight factor, vacancy factor and provisional factor**: each 1.
- **On-peak share**: 0.

## The calculation

1. **Estimated export kWh.** The estimate basis multiplied by the daylight factor, the vacancy factor and the provisional factor, multiplied together in that order on the kWh total, and rounded to a whole kWh once at the end.
2. **On-peak and off-peak kWh.** The estimated on-peak export kWh are the estimated export kWh multiplied by the on-peak share, rounded to a whole kWh; the estimated off-peak export kWh are the rest.
3. **Valuation.** Each estimated kWh is valued at the rate recorded on the preceding export credit for the same period of day: on-peak kWh at its on-peak rate, off-peak kWh at its off-peak rate.
4. **Estimated export credit.** The sum of the two valued parts, rounded to the cent.

## Rounding points

| Quantity | Rounded |
|---|---|
| Estimated export kWh | To a whole kWh, once, after all multiplications |
| Estimated on-peak export kWh | To a whole kWh |
| Estimated export credit | To the cent, on the sum |

## Hypothetical worked figure

Hypothetical inputs: the preceding export credit records 120 kWh on-peak and 380 kWh off-peak, at 0.09280 on-peak and 0.04120 off-peak USD per kWh.

- Estimate basis: 500 kWh. Estimated export kWh: 500 multiplied by 1, by 1 and by 1, that is 500.
- On-peak: 500 multiplied by 0, that is 0 kWh; off-peak: 500 kWh.
- Estimated export credit: 500 multiplied by 0.04120, that is 20.60, recorded with the two rates 0.09280 and 0.04120.

title: Export Credits for Estimated-Read Billing Periods — Net Energy Metering Billing Standard
content:
**Scope.** Under Net Energy Metering, this standard governs the export credit of a billing period whose service bill was issued on an estimated closing read and which has no export credit in the net metering history of an operating agreement. The estimated period is the period of the most recent service bill of the hosting service agreement, and the preceding period is the period of the most recent export credit in the net metering history.

**What is banked.** One estimated export credit is banked for that period, recording the estimated on-peak and off-peak export kWh, the two rates used and the amount, dated to the estimated period's billing period end, and it is trued up at the next actual read.

**Rates and timing.** The estimated export credit is fixed only after the most recent export credit in the net metering history carries the per-kWh rates that the revaluation of export credits fixes for it. Until the most recent export credit in the history carries those rates, the estimated export credit is not fixed.

## The period covered at a glance

| Element | Rule |
|---|---|
| Period credited | The billing period of the hosting service agreement's most recent service bill, issued on an estimated closing read, with no export credit in the net metering history |
| Agreement | In operating status |
| Number of credits | One estimated export credit for that period |
| Date of the credit | The estimated period's billing period end |
| Recorded on the credit | Estimated on-peak and off-peak export kWh, the two rates used, the amount |
| Later | Trued up at the next actual read |

After booking, the net metering history lists the new export credit for that billing period and the agreement's credit bank balance is higher by its amount.

## Banking the estimated credit — `book_estimated_export_credit_93ce1e35`

**Capability.** The tool adds one export credit entry to the agreement's net metering history for a billing period that has none, recording the estimated on-peak and off-peak export kWh, the two per-kWh rates used and the dollar amount, dated to the billing period end; the agreement's banked credit rises by that amount.

**How it is invoked.** It is a representative's tool: the representative unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `nem_agreement_id` | Reference number of the net metering agreement (interconnection application number), read from the net metering agreement lookup | Identifier |
| `billing_period_end` | Last day of the billing period the credit belongs to, copied from the billing period end printed on the service bill for that period | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `export_kwh_on_peak` | Estimated kWh exported in on-peak hours | Non-negative whole kWh; 0 when none |
| `export_kwh_off_peak` | Estimated kWh exported in all other hours | Non-negative whole kWh |
| `credit_rate_on_peak` | Rate applied to the on-peak kWh | USD per kWh, decimal with 5 decimal places |
| `credit_rate_off_peak` | Rate applied to the off-peak kWh | USD per kWh, decimal with 5 decimal places |
| `estimated_credit_usd` | Dollar amount of the estimated export credit | USD, positive decimal with 2 decimal places, rounded to the cent |

**Return.** On success the receipt carries `status` "banked"; `nem_ledger_id`, the reference number of the new export credit entry; `nem_agreement_id`; `billing_period_end` in YYYY-MM-DD; `amount`, the credit in USD with 2 decimals; and `credit_bank_balance`, the agreement's banked credit in USD with 2 decimals after the entry.

title: Billing Operations Rule — Estimated-Read Holdback at a Net Energy Metering Move-Out
content:
When the latest bill of the Electric Service Agreement hosting a Net Energy Metering system was issued on an estimated closing read, part of the most recent export credit is held back from the move-out payout.

**Rule.** When the most recent service bill of the hosting service agreement is a final bill issued on an estimated closing read, the holdback share is the final-estimate holdback share of 0.24. When that bill is a regular bill issued on an estimated closing read, it is the regular-estimate holdback share of 0.10. Otherwise no holdback applies. The estimated-read holdback is the export credit of the most recent billing period in the net metering history multiplied by the holdback share, rounded to the cent.

**Records read.** The bill kind (regular or final) and the read type of the most recent service bill of the hosting Electric Service Agreement; the amount of the export credit with the latest billing period end in the net metering history.

## Holdback share

| Most recent service bill | Closing read | Holdback share |
|---|---|---|
| Final bill | Estimated | 0.24 |
| Regular bill | Estimated | 0.10 |
| Final or regular bill | Actual or customer read | None |

## Hypothetical worked cases

Hypothetical input: the most recent export credit is 38.40.

- Final bill on an estimated read: 38.40 multiplied by 0.24 is 9.216, a holdback of 9.22.
- Regular bill on an estimated read: 38.40 multiplied by 0.10, a holdback of 3.84.
- Bill on an actual read: no holdback.

title: Estimated-Read Reserve Held Back from Expiring Net Energy Metering Credit
content:
At the anniversary expiry of carried Net Energy Metering credit, a reserve is held back when bills of the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system were issued on estimated closing reads during the past year.

**Rule.** When two or more bills of the hosting service agreement dated in the 12 months before the expiry were issued on an estimated closing read, there are two reserve months. When exactly one was, there is one reserve month. Otherwise no reserve is held. The reserve is the reserve months multiplied by the credit applied in the closing true-up year divided by 12, rounded to the cent.

**Records read.** The read type and bill date of each service bill of the hosting Electric Service Agreement; the credit applied to bills for the billing periods of the closing true-up year, from the net metering history.

## Reserve months

| Bills dated in the 12 months before the expiry issued on an estimated closing read | Reserve months |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | 2 |
| Exactly 1 | 1 |
| None | No reserve |

## Hypothetical worked cases

Hypothetical input: credit applied in the closing true-up year of 470.00.

- One estimated bill: 1 multiplied by 470.00 divided by 12 is 39.1667, a reserve of 39.17.
- Three estimated bills: 2 multiplied by 470.00 divided by 12 is 78.3333, a reserve of 78.33.
- No estimated bill: no reserve.

title: Settlement Worksheet — Expired Carried Credit at a Net Energy Metering Anniversary True-Up
content:
This worksheet fixes the amount of carried credit that expires at the anniversary true-up of a Net Energy Metering agreement.

## Definitions

- **Closing true-up year**: the billing periods ended in the 12 whole months before the expiry is booked.
- **Year's export credits**: the export credits banked for the periods of the closing true-up year, from the net metering history.
- **Year's applied credit**: the credit applied to bills for those periods, from the net metering history.
- **Carried credit**: the credit bank balance recorded on the agreement, less the year's export credits, plus the year's applied credit.
- **Carried credit used**: the lesser of the carried credit and the year's applied credit.
- **Reserve**: the reserve months multiplied by the year's applied credit divided by 12, rounded to the cent. There are no reserve months, so the reserve is zero.
- **Expiry share**: 1. **Exempt amount**: none.

## The amount

The expired carried credit is the carried credit less the carried credit used and less the reserve, multiplied by the expiry share, less the exempt amount, rounded to the cent once and never below zero. An expired carried credit of zero books nothing.

## Hypothetical worked figures

| | Case A | Case B |
|---|---|---|
| Credit bank balance | 610.00 | 410.00 |
| Year's export credits | 420.00 | 520.00 |
| Year's applied credit | 150.00 | 300.00 |
| Carried credit | 340.00 | 190.00 |
| Carried credit used | 150.00 | 190.00 |
| Expired carried credit | 190.00 | 0.00, nothing booked |

In Case A the carried credit of 340.00 is 610.00 less 420.00 plus 150.00; the year's bills used 150.00 of it, and 190.00 expires.

title: Revaluation of Retail-Valued Export Credits — Net Energy Metering
content:
Under Net Energy Metering, this rule governs the revaluation of the most recent export credit banked under an agreement whose rider values exports at a retail rate: Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering, Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering and Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering.

## When an export credit is revalued

- When the per-kWh rates recorded on that export credit are not the rates this rule fixes, the credit is revalued.
- An export credit banked for a billing period whose service bill was issued on an estimated closing read is never revalued; it is trued up at the next actual read.
- A revaluation is booked only for an agreement in operating status, and it changes no other export credit.

## Effect of a revaluation

The revalued export credit and its two revalued rates replace the amount and the two rates recorded on that same export credit. The export kWh recorded on it stay as recorded. The bank moves by the difference between the revalued export credit and the amount it replaces.

| Revalued export credit compared with the amount recorded | Credit bank balance |
|---|---|
| Higher | Rises by the difference |
| Lower | Falls by the difference |

Afterwards the net metering history shows that export credit with its revalued rates and amount, and the agreement shows the adjusted bank. Hypothetical illustration: an export credit recorded at 41.30 and revalued at 44.12 raises the bank by 2.82.

## Recording the revaluation — `revalue_export_credit_a4b62fb5`

**Capability.** The tool replaces the two per-kWh rates and the dollar amount recorded on one existing export credit entry with the revalued rates and amount, leaves the entry's export kWh unchanged, and moves the banked credit of the agreement that owns the entry by the difference between the revalued amount and the amount previously recorded.

**How it is invoked.** It is a representative's tool: the representative unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `nem_agreement_id` | Reference number of the net metering agreement (interconnection application number) that owns the entry, read from the net metering agreement lookup | Identifier |
| `nem_ledger_id` | Reference number of the export credit entry being revalued, read from the net metering history lookup of that agreement | Identifier |
| `credit_rate_on_peak` | Revalued rate applied to the entry's on-peak export kWh | USD per kWh, decimal with 5 decimal places, rounded half up to 5 places; 0.00000 when no on-peak rate applies |
| `credit_rate_off_peak` | Revalued rate applied to the entry's off-peak export kWh | USD per kWh, decimal with 5 decimal places, rounded half up to 5 places |
| `revalued_credit_usd` | Revalued dollar amount of the export credit | USD, positive decimal with 2 decimal places, rounded to the cent |

**Return.** On success the receipt carries `status` "revalued"; `nem_ledger_id`, the entry revalued; `nem_agreement_id`, the agreement whose bank moved; `previous_amount` and `revalued_amount`, the old and new entry amounts in USD with 2 decimals; `credit_rate_on_peak` and `credit_rate_off_peak`, the stored rates in USD per kWh with 5 decimals; and `credit_bank_balance`, the agreement's banked credit in USD with 2 decimals after the change.

title: Export Credit Rate Sheet — Net Energy Metering Riders
content:
Each Net Energy Metering rider values exported kWh on one of three bases. This sheet gives each rider's basis, its non-bypassable charge, its avoided-cost export rates, the hours that count as on-peak for exports, the years the export rates stay fixed, and how amounts are rounded and estimated.

## Valuation basis and rates

| Rider | Valuation basis | Non-bypassable charge (USD per kWh) | On-peak export rate (USD per kWh) | Off-peak export rate (USD per kWh) | Years the export rates stay fixed after permission to operate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering | Retail energy rate | 0.00000 | 0.00000 | 0.00000 | 0 |
| Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering | Retail energy rate less the non-bypassable charge | 0.02215 | 0.00000 | 0.00000 | 0 |
| Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff | Avoided-cost export rate | 0.00000 | 0.09280 | 0.04120 | 9 |
| Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff | Avoided-cost export rate | 0.00000 | 0.08640 | 0.03875 | 9 |
| Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering | Retail energy rate less the non-bypassable charge | 0.02215 | 0.00000 | 0.00000 | 0 |
| Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff | Avoided-cost export rate | 0.00000 | 0.07915 | 0.03560 | 9 |

The avoided-cost export rates show 0.00000 under the three retail-based riders, and the rate lock shows 0 years for them, because those riders do not value exports at avoided-cost rates. The non-bypassable charge is used only where the basis is the retail energy rate less the non-bypassable charge.

## Export on-peak window

| Rider | Hours whose exports count as on-peak |
|---|---|
| Rider NEM-L, Rider NEM-R and Rider NEM-A | The on-peak hours of the service agreement's rate schedule; every hour is off-peak on flat schedules |
| Rider NBT-R, Rider NBT-C and Rider NBT-L | 15:00-20:00 Monday-Friday except company holidays, whatever the service agreement's rate schedule |

## Rounding and estimated reads

| Rider | Rounding of export credit amounts | Exports on a bill with an estimated read |
|---|---|---|
| All six riders | The credit amount is rounded to the cent per bill | Exports are estimated by the same method as deliveries and trued up at the next actual read |

## Notes to the sheet

- The three Rider NBT riders are the net billing riders valued at avoided-cost export rates; their export window is fixed at 15:00-20:00 on weekdays except company holidays, even on a flat schedule.
- Rider NEM-L values each exported kWh at the retail energy rate; Rider NEM-R and Rider NEM-A at the retail energy rate less 0.02215 USD per kWh.

title: Meter Data Estimation Rules — Basis of Estimated Export kWh for Net Energy Metering
content:
When a Net Energy Metering export credit is estimated for a billing period closed on an estimated read, the estimate basis — the export kWh total that the estimate starts from — depends on the kind of service bill issued for the estimated period on the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system and on how the preceding period's bill was read.

**Rule.** When the estimated period's bill is a final bill, the basis is the preceding period's total export kWh multiplied by the days in the estimated period divided by the days in the preceding period, each period counted from its first day through its last day with both days included, the quotient rounded to four decimals. When the estimated period's bill is a regular bill and the preceding period's bill was also issued on an estimated closing read, the basis is the average total export kWh of the export credits banked for billing periods ended in the 3 months before the booking, rounded to two decimals. Otherwise the basis is the preceding period's total export kWh carried over unscaled.

**Records read.** The estimated period is the period of the most recent service bill of the hosting Electric Service Agreement; its bill kind (regular or final) and its billing period start and end are those printed on that bill. The preceding period is the period of the most recent export credit in the net metering history; the preceding period's bill is the service bill whose billing period ends on that credit's billing period end, and its read type and billing period start are read from it. The preceding period's total export kWh are the on-peak plus off-peak export kWh recorded on that credit.

## Basis by bill

| Estimated period's bill | Preceding period's bill | Estimate basis |
|---|---|---|
| Final bill | Any read | Preceding total export kWh multiplied by the day ratio, the ratio rounded to four decimals |
| Regular bill | Issued on an estimated closing read | Average total export kWh of the export credits for billing periods ended in the 3 months before the booking, rounded to two decimals |
| Regular bill | Issued on an actual read or a customer read | Preceding total export kWh, unscaled |

## Hypothetical worked cases

- **Final bill.** Preceding period 1 March through 31 March (31 days) with 620 kWh exported; estimated final-bill period 1 April through 17 April (17 days). The ratio 17 divided by 31 is 0.548387, rounded to 0.5484; the basis is 620 multiplied by 0.5484, that is 340.008 kWh.
- **Second estimated read in a row.** Export credits for billing periods ended in the 3 months before the booking total 410, 455 and 432 kWh: their average, 1297 divided by 3, is 432.333, so the basis is 432.33 kWh.
- **Regular bill after an actual read.** The preceding period's 515 kWh are carried over as the basis.

title: Commercial Rider Terms — Fixed Retention at the Net Energy Metering Anniversary Cash-Out
content:
Under the business Net Energy Metering riders — Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff, Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering and Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff — a fixed amount is retained in the bank at the anniversary cash-out, set by whether the rate schedule of the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system bills a demand charge.

**Rule.** For a business rider on a schedule with a demand charge, the fixed retention is the demand-schedule fixed retention of 200.00. For a business rider on a schedule without a demand charge, it is the general-service fixed retention of 120.00. Under a residential rider no fixed retention applies.

**Records read.** The customer class of the rider; the demand charge per kW of the hosting service agreement's rate schedule, where a demand charge of 0.00 means the schedule bills none.

## Fixed retention

| Rider | Hosting schedule | Fixed retention (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| Business rider | Bills a demand charge | 200.00 |
| Business rider | Bills no demand charge | 120.00 |
| Residential rider | Any | None |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A Rider NBT-C agreement hosted on a schedule with a demand charge per kW above zero: 200.00 retained.
- A Rider NBT-C agreement hosted on a schedule whose demand charge is 0.00: 120.00 retained.
- A Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering agreement: no fixed retention.

title: Residential Rider Terms — Full-Value Months by Space Heating at Net Energy Metering Move-Out
content:
At a move-out termination under a residential Net Energy Metering rider (Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering, Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering or Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff), the number of full-value months depends on the space heating of the premises.

**Rule.** For a residential rider with electric space heating at the premises, the full-value months are the electric-heat month count of 1.5. For a residential rider with space heating that is not electric, they are the other-heat month count of 1.0. An agreement under a business rider takes neither heating-based count.

**Records read.** The primary space-heating source of the premises, electric or non-electric, as recorded on the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system; the customer class of the rider.

## Full-value months

| Rider | Space heating at the premises | Full-value months |
|---|---|---|
| Residential rider | Electric | 1.5 |
| Residential rider | Not electric | 1.0 |
| Business rider | Any | No heating-based count |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A Rider NBT-R agreement at a premises recorded with electric space heating: 1.5 full-value months.
- A Rider NEM-R agreement at a premises recorded with non-electric space heating: 1.0 full-value month.
- A Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff agreement: no heating-based count, whatever the heating.

title: Monthly Grid Access Charge on Net Energy Metering Agreements
content:
**Rule.** Where the rider's grid access charge per kW is above zero, every billing period of an operating Net Energy Metering agreement is charged the grid access charge per kW multiplied by the system's nameplate capacity in kW AC, rounded to the cent, dated the billing period end. The charge is never offset by banked credit. One charge is booked per billing period.

The rate per kW is the rider's figure in its grid access charge rates; the capacity is the nameplate capacity recorded on the agreement.

## Features of the charge

| Feature | Rule |
|---|---|
| Applies | Riders with a grid access charge above zero, agreements in operating status |
| Amount | Rate per kW multiplied by nameplate kW AC, rounded to the cent |
| Date | The billing period end |
| Frequency | One per billing period of the agreement, checked against the company's records for that period |
| Banked credit | Never offsets it |

## Worked figures

- Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff, 7.6 kW AC: 0.93 multiplied by 7.6 is 7.068, charged as 7.07 each billing period.
- Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff, 48.0 kW AC: 0.93 multiplied by 48.0, charged as 44.64.
- Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff, 250.0 kW AC: 1.85 multiplied by 250.0, charged as 462.50.
- Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering, any size: the rider's rate is 0.00, so no charge is booked.

title: Grid Access Charge Rates — Net Energy Metering Riders
content:
The grid access charge is a monthly charge per kW AC of nameplate capacity on certain Net Energy Metering riders. A rate of 0.00 means the rider carries no grid access charge.

| Rider | Grid access charge (USD per kW AC per month) |
|---|---|
| Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering | 0.00 (none) |
| Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering | 0.00 (none) |
| Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff | 0.93 |

| Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering | 0.00 (none) |

Only the three net billing riders carry the charge: 0.93 under Rider NBT-R and Rider NBT-C, and 1.85 under Rider NBT-L.

title: Schedule of Exempt Amounts — Grid Access Charges and Expiring Net Energy Metering Credit
content:
Under the Net Energy Metering riders valued at the avoided-cost export rates — Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff, Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff and Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff — an exempt amount of carried credit is spared at the anniversary expiry, sized by the grid access charges booked on the agreement over the past year.

**Rule.** When the rider values exports at the avoided-cost export rates and the grid access charges booked for billing periods ended in the 12 months before the expiry total at least the large-system charge total of 300.00, the exempt amount is the large-system exempt amount of 25.00. When the rider values exports at the avoided-cost export rates and those charges total less than 300.00, it is the small-system exempt amount of 10.00. Under a retail-valued rider no exempt amount applies.

**Records read.** The grid access charges in the agreement's net metering history whose billing periods ended in the 12 months before the expiry.

## Exempt amount

| Rider | Grid access charges of the 12 months | Exempt amount (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| Avoided-cost rider | 300.00 or more | 25.00 |
| Avoided-cost rider | Less than 300.00 | 10.00 |
| Retail-valued rider | Any | None |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- Twelve monthly grid access charges of 25.11 total 301.32: at least 300.00, so 25.00.
- Twelve charges of 24.99 total 299.88: less than 300.00, so 10.00.
- Twelve charges of exactly 25.00 total 300.00: at least 300.00, so 25.00.
