title: Interconnection Review, Approval Validity and Permission to Operate — Net Energy Metering
content:
These rules govern an application under Net Energy Metering from review to permission to operate: the review, rejection, approval, approval validity, expiry and withdrawal of the application.

## Rules of the interconnection desk

1. **Review.** A complete application is reviewed within the rider's review period in business days.
2. **Deficient applications.** A deficient application not completed within the rider's completion period in business days, counted from the deficiency notice, is rejected with the rejection reason "incomplete application". An application outside the size, type or rider limits is rejected with the matching reason.
3. **Certifications.** Applicants under riders with a liability insurance minimum or an external disconnect switch requirement must certify both before approval.
4. **Conditions of permission to operate.** Permission to operate requires a bidirectional meter in service at the address and, where the rider requires inspection, a passed inspection.
5. **Approval validity.** Permission to operate may be issued only no later than the approval validity period after the approval date. The period is counted in calendar months from the approval date, ending on the same day of the month the rider's approval validity months later, or on the last day of a shorter month, and that last day is still in time.
6. **Expiry.** An approval not followed by permission to operate in time expires on the next day, and the customer must apply again under the rider then open.
7. **True-up month.** The true-up month is the calendar month of the permission to operate date.
8. **Withdrawal.** The customer may withdraw an application in applied or approved status at any time; withdrawal is the customer's own decision.

The approval date is the date recorded on the agreement; the review periods, completion periods, validity months and inspection requirement are those of the rider.

## The validity period on the calendar

| Approval date | Validity | Last day permission to operate may be issued | Approval expires on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 March | 12 months | 10 March of the next year | 11 March of the next year |
| 31 January | 12 months | 31 January of the next year | 1 February of the next year |
| 31 August | 18 months | The last day of February eighteen months later (a shorter month) | 1 March following |
| 30 June | 24 months | 30 June two years later | 1 July two years later |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- Approval on 15 May under a 12-month validity. Permission to operate issued on 15 May of the next year is in time, because the last day is included. Issued on 16 May of the next year it is not; the approval expired on that day.
- Approval on 31 October under a 12-month validity. The period ends on 31 October of the next year; issuing on 30 October or 31 October is in time.

## Withdrawal at a glance

| Status of the agreement | Customer may withdraw |
|---|---|
| Applied | Yes |
| Approved | Yes |
| Operating | Withdrawal no longer applies; an operating agreement ends by termination |

title: Metering Charges — Meter Reconfiguration on Ending a Net Energy Metering Agreement
content:
When a Net Energy Metering agreement is ended at the customer's request, a meter reconfiguration charge is deducted from the bank according to the type of Metering Service meter in service at the address.

**Rule.** When the meter in service at the address is an AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter, the meter reconfiguration charge is the three-phase reconfiguration charge of 60.00. When the meter in service is an AMI Bidirectional Net Meter, it is the single-phase reconfiguration charge of 35.00. Otherwise, for interval demand and primary metering installations that are reprogrammed remotely, there is none.

**Records read.** The Metering Service installation in service at the address of the service agreement hosting the system, and its meter type.

## Charge by meter in service

| Meter in service at the address | Reconfiguration charge (USD) |
|---|---|
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | 60.00 |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | 35.00 |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter or Primary Metering Installation (reprogrammed remotely) | None |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A home whose Metering Service record shows an AMI Bidirectional Net Meter in service: 35.00.
- A shop whose record shows an AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter in service: 60.00.
- A plant whose record shows a Primary Metering Installation in service: no charge.

title: Net Energy Metering Agreement Terms: Grandfathering, Capacity Modifications and Sale of the Premises
content:
These terms of each Net Energy Metering rider govern how long the agreement keeps the rider's credit terms, how much capacity may be added without a new application, whether any increase forfeits the legacy terms, and what happens to the agreement and the bank when the premises are sold.

## Grandfathering and modifications

| Rider | Years after permission to operate the agreement keeps the rider's credit terms | Largest capacity increase through a modification, as a fraction of approved capacity | Any capacity increase moves the agreement off the rider |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering | 20 | 0.10 (10 percent) | Yes |
| Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering | 20 | 0.10 (10 percent) | No |
| Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff | 9 | 0.10 (10 percent) | No |
| Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff | 9 | 0.10 (10 percent) | No |
| Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering | 20 | 0.10 (10 percent) | No |
| Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff | 9 | 0.10 (10 percent) | No |

Under Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering any capacity increase moves the agreement to the rider open for new applications for the customer's class.

## Sale of the premises

| Rider | Agreement transfers to a new owner who starts service at the address | Seller's bank on transfer |
|---|---|---|
| All six riders | Yes | The seller's bank is settled under the rider's termination disposition at transfer |

## Points of the terms

- Hypothetical illustration: an operating 8.0 kW AC system under Rider NEM-R may be modified up to 8.8 kW AC, the approved capacity plus 10 percent of it; the same increase under Rider NEM-L moves the agreement off the legacy rider.

title: Net Energy Metering Agreement Terms — Modification, Transfer on Sale and Termination
content:
## Terms in force

**Modification.** An operating Net Energy Metering agreement may increase its capacity by no more than the rider's modification limit, as a fraction of the approved capacity, through a modification, within the rider's size limits. A larger increase requires a new application under the rider then open, and under a rider whose modifications lose grandfathering any increase does. Modifications are made only on an agreement in operating status.

**Transfer on sale.** When the premises are sold and the rider allows transfer on sale, the agreement moves to the buyer's service agreement at the same address once the buyer has started service. The seller's bank is settled under the rider's disposition on sale before the move, and the true-up month is unchanged.

**Termination.** Termination is the customer's decision, or follows the closure of the service agreement when no transfer applies.

**Clause no longer in force.** The clause providing that the bank is then settled under the rider's termination disposition is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current termination settlement basis.

The status of the agreement is read from the company's records before a modification or a transfer is made; only an agreement in operating status qualifies for either.

## Capacity increases (hypothetical approved capacity of 10.0 kW AC, modification limit of 10 percent)

| New capacity | Rider whose modifications do not lose grandfathering | Rider whose modifications lose grandfathering |
|---|---|---|
| 11.0 kW AC | Modification, provided it stays within the rider's size limits | New application under the rider then open |
| 11.1 kW AC | New application under the rider then open | New application under the rider then open |

## Transfer on sale at a glance

| Element | Rule |
|---|---|
| Who receives the agreement | The buyer, on the buyer's service agreement at the same address |
| When | Once the buyer has started service |
| Seller's bank | Settled under the rider's disposition on sale, before the move |
| True-up month | Unchanged |

title: Billing Operations Standard — Monthly Export Credits under Net Energy Metering
content:
**Standard in force.** Each billing period of an operating Net Energy Metering agreement banks one export credit. Under a rider whose basis is the avoided-cost export rate, each exported kWh is valued at the rider's on-peak export rate or off-peak export rate. The rates used are recorded on the credit, and the amount is rounded to the cent. Export credits are banked only for an agreement in operating status, and energy exported from a battery charged from the grid earns no credit where the rider does not allow grid-charged battery energy to be exported for credit.

**Amount of the credit.** The export credit is the on-peak export kWh multiplied by the on-peak rate, plus the off-peak export kWh multiplied by the off-peak rate, the sum rounded to the cent.

**Clauses no longer in force.** Two clauses of this standard are no longer in force and have been superseded by the current basis:

- the clause providing that exported kWh are split into on-peak and off-peak exports under the rider's export on-peak window;
- the clause providing that, under the retail energy rate basis, each kWh is valued at the service schedule's energy rate for the same season and period, and under the retail energy rate less the non-bypassable charge basis, at that rate less the rider's non-bypassable charge.

## Conditions of an export credit

| Condition | Effect |
|---|---|
| Agreement in operating status (company records, read before the credit is booked) | One export credit per billing period |
| Agreement in applied, approved or any closed status | No export credit is banked |
| Energy exported from a battery charged from the grid, under a rider that does not allow its export for credit | That energy earns no credit |

## What each export credit records

The billing period it belongs to, the on-peak export kWh, the off-peak export kWh, the rate applied to each, and the amount banked.

## Hypothetical worked credit

Hypothetical inputs: an operating agreement under an avoided-cost rider with an on-peak export rate of 0.09280 and an off-peak export rate of 0.04120 USD per kWh; 118 kWh exported on-peak and 402 kWh off-peak in the billing period.

- On-peak value: 118 multiplied by 0.09280 is 10.9504.
- Off-peak value: 402 multiplied by 0.04120 is 16.5624.
- The sum is 27.5128, rounded to the cent: an export credit of 27.51, with both rates recorded on the credit.

title: Settlement Worksheet — Net Energy Metering Move-Out Payout and Surrendered Amount
content:
This worksheet fixes the move-out payout and the surrendered amount when a Net Energy Metering agreement ends because the customer stops electric service at the address.

## Inputs

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| Bank | The credit bank balance recorded on the agreement when the termination is recorded |
| Average monthly offsettable charges | The energy charge plus the Power Supply Cost Recovery charge of the most recent service bill of the hosting service agreement |
| Full-value months | 0.5 months |
| Tenure months | None |
| Surplus share | 1 |
| Staying uplift | None |
| Holdback share | 0 |

## The calculation

1. **Full-value limit**: the average monthly offsettable charges multiplied by the sum of the full-value months and the tenure months, rounded to the cent.
2. **Full-value portion**: the lesser of the bank and the full-value limit.
3. **Surplus**: the bank less the full-value portion.
4. **Paid surplus**: the surplus multiplied by the sum of the surplus share and the staying uplift, rounded to the cent.
5. **Estimated-read holdback**: the export credit of the most recent billing period in the net metering history multiplied by the holdback share, rounded to the cent.
6. **Move-out payout**: the full-value portion plus the paid surplus less the estimated-read holdback, rounded to the cent.
7. **Surrendered amount**: the bank less the move-out payout.

## Hypothetical worked figure

Hypothetical inputs: a bank of 612.40; a most recent service bill with an energy charge of 74.18 and a Power Supply Cost Recovery charge of 3.02.

- Average monthly offsettable charges: 77.20.
- Full-value limit: 77.20 multiplied by 0.5, that is 38.60; full-value portion 38.60.
- Surplus: 612.40 less 38.60, that is 573.80; paid surplus 573.80 multiplied by 1, that is 573.80.
- Holdback: 0.00.
- Move-out payout: 38.60 plus 573.80, that is 612.40; surrendered amount 0.00.

A bank smaller than the full-value limit is taken in full as the full-value portion, and the surplus is then zero.

title: Customer Care Knowledge Article — Ending Net Energy Metering When Electric Service Stops at the Address
content:
**Scope.** Under Net Energy Metering, this rule governs the customer's own decision to end an operating net metering agreement because they are stopping electric service at the address and no transfer to a buyer applies, under a rider whose termination disposition is cash out.

**Outside this rule.** A move-out whose final bill is dated in the agreement's true-up month is outside this rule. An agreement under a rider whose termination disposition is forfeit is outside this rule; its bank is forfeited at termination as the base rule provides.

**When the settlement is fixed.** The move-out settlement is not fixed until every billing period billed on the hosting service agreement since permission to operate has an export credit in the net metering history. While any such billing period has no export credit in the history, the move-out settlement is not fixed.

**Settlement.** At a move-out termination under a rider whose termination disposition is cash out, the move-out payout is paid by check and the rest of the bank is surrendered, so the bank stands at zero once the agreement is terminated. This rule settles a move-out payout of at least the rider's check minimum; a smaller move-out payout is credited to the service agreement as the base rule provides.

## Coverage at a glance

| Situation | Under this rule |
|---|---|
| Customer stops electric service at the address, no transfer to a buyer, operating agreement, cash-out termination disposition, final bill not dated in the true-up month | Yes |
| Final bill dated in the agreement's true-up month | No |
| Rider whose termination disposition is forfeit | No; the bank is forfeited at termination |
| Move-out payout below the rider's check minimum | No; credited to the service agreement |

## Ending the agreement — `end_net_metering_at_move_out_41499158`

**Capability.** The customer ends their operating net metering agreement: the agreement becomes terminated as of the day the tool is run, the move-out payout is recorded as a termination settlement paid by check, any part of the bank not paid is recorded as surrendered at termination, and the agreement's banked credit becomes 0.00. Afterwards the agreement shows terminated status and the history shows the check payout, and the surrendered amount when it is above zero.

**How it is invoked.** This is the customer's own tool. The representative unlocks it with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and hands it over; the customer themselves runs it with `call_user_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `nem_agreement_id` | Reference number of the customer's net metering agreement, as given to the customer by the representative from the agreement lookup | Identifier |
| `payout_usd` | Move-out payout to be sent by check, exactly as the representative states it | USD, positive decimal with 2 decimal places |
| `surrendered_usd` | Part of the bank that is not paid and is surrendered, exactly as the representative states it | USD, decimal with 2 decimal places; 0.00 when nothing is surrendered |

**Return.** On success the receipt carries `status` "terminated"; `nem_agreement_id`; `termination_date`, the day's date in YYYY-MM-DD; `payout_reference`, the reference number of the check payout entry; `payout_amount` and `surrendered_amount` in USD with 2 decimals; and `credit_bank_balance`, 0.00 after settlement.

title: Rider NEM-R and Rider NEM-A — Phase-In of the Non-Bypassable Charge on Revalued Export Credits (Net Energy Metering)
content:
Under the Net Energy Metering riders whose basis is the retail energy rate less the non-bypassable charge — Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering and Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering, each with a non-bypassable charge of 0.02215 USD per kWh — the charge deducted from a revalued export rate is phased in over the agreement's first months of operation.

**Rule.** Under the retail-rate-less-non-bypassable-charge basis, when the whole calendar months from the permission to operate date to the export credit's billing period end are at least the full-charge month count of 24, the rider's non-bypassable charge is deducted in full. Under that basis, when those months are fewer than 24, the rider's non-bypassable charge multiplied by the phase-in share of 0.50, rounded to five decimals, is deducted. Otherwise nothing is deducted.

The deduction applies to both revalued rates. The permission to operate date is the date recorded on the agreement; the billing period end is that of the export credit revalued.

## Deduction by months in operation

| Rider basis | Whole calendar months from permission to operate to the billing period end | Non-bypassable charge deducted |
|---|---|---|
| Retail energy rate less the non-bypassable charge | 24 or more | 0.02215, in full |
| Retail energy rate less the non-bypassable charge | Fewer than 24 | 0.02215 multiplied by 0.50 is 0.011075, rounded to 0.01108 |
| Retail energy rate (Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering) | Any | Nothing |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- Permission to operate on 10 March of one year; export credit for a billing period ending 9 March two years later: 23 whole months, so 0.01108 is deducted.
- The same agreement, billing period ending 10 March two years later: 24 whole months, so 0.02215 is deducted in full.

title: On-Peak Share of Estimated Net Energy Metering Exports
content:
The estimated export kWh of a Net Energy Metering export credit are divided between on-peak and off-peak by an on-peak share, which depends on whether the export window of the rider has on-peak hours and on the season of the estimated period's bill.

**When the export window has on-peak hours.** The export window has on-peak hours under every rider valued at the avoided-cost export rates — Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff, Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff and Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff — and, under the retail-valued riders — Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering, Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering and Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering — when the rate schedule of the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system has on-peak hours.

**Rule.** When the export window has on-peak hours and the estimated period's bill is a winter bill, the on-peak share is the winter on-peak share of 0.16. When the export window has on-peak hours and the estimated period's bill is a summer bill, the on-peak share is the preceding export credit's on-peak export kWh divided by its total export kWh, rounded to four decimals. When the export window has no on-peak hours, no on-peak share arises.

The estimated period's bill is the most recent service bill of the hosting Electric Service Agreement, and its season is the pricing season printed on it. The preceding export credit is the most recent export credit in the net metering history.

## On-peak share

| Rider | Hosting schedule | Estimated period's bill | On-peak share |
|---|---|---|---|
| Avoided-cost rider | Any | Winter | 0.16 |
| Avoided-cost rider | Any | Summer | Preceding credit's on-peak kWh divided by its total, to four decimals |
| Retail-valued rider | Has on-peak hours | Winter | 0.16 |
| Retail-valued rider | Has on-peak hours | Summer | Preceding credit's on-peak kWh divided by its total, to four decimals |
| Retail-valued rider | No on-peak hours (flat) | Any | No on-peak share |

## Hypothetical worked case

Hypothetical inputs: a preceding export credit of 132 kWh on-peak and 468 kWh off-peak. On a summer bill the share is 132 divided by 600, that is 0.2200; on a winter bill it is 0.16.

title: Net Energy Metering Agreements Held per Service Agreement
content:
**Rule.** A customer may hold Net Energy Metering agreements at several service agreements, one per service agreement. An application is taken for a service agreement only where no other Net Energy Metering agreement on the same service agreement is in applied, approved or operating status. A second system at the same premises is added by modification, or by a new application after the first agreement terminates.

**Number per customer.** There is no limit on the number of Net Energy Metering agreements one customer may hold across different service agreements; the only limit is one open agreement per service agreement.

## What the records must show

The test is decided from the company's records of the service agreement, not from what the customer says, and it is read before the application is taken. The agreements compared are those on the same service agreement as the new application.

| Other agreement on the same service agreement | A new application on that service agreement |
|---|---|
| None | May be taken |
| One in applied status | Not taken |
| One in approved status | Not taken |
| One in operating status | Not taken |
| Only agreements in rejected, withdrawn, expired or terminated status | May be taken |

## Points of judgement

- **A customer with solar at two addresses.** Each address has its own service agreement, so each may hold its own agreement; the second address is not blocked by the first.
- **A second array on the same roof.** While the first agreement is operating, the added system comes in by modification of that agreement. A separate new application at that service agreement is possible only once the first agreement has terminated.
- **An earlier application that was rejected or has expired.** It is no longer in applied, approved or operating status, so it does not stand in the way of a new application on the same service agreement.

title: Settlement Desk Note — Open-Period Holdback on Ending Net Energy Metering at the Customer's Request
content:
When a customer ends a Net Energy Metering agreement while keeping electric service, part of the most recent export credit is held back for the open billing period when the rate schedule of the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system has on-peak hours.

**Rule.** When the most recent service bill of the hosting service agreement is a summer bill and its schedule has on-peak hours, the holdback share is the summer holdback share of 0.20. When that bill is a winter bill and the schedule has on-peak hours, it is the winter holdback share of 0.10. Otherwise no holdback applies. The open-period holdback is the export credit of the most recent billing period in the net metering history multiplied by the holdback share, rounded to the cent.

**Records read.** The pricing season printed on the most recent service bill of the hosting Electric Service Agreement; whether that agreement's rate schedule has on-peak hours; the export credit with the latest billing period end in the net metering history.

## Holdback share

| Most recent service bill | Hosting schedule | Holdback share |
|---|---|---|
| Summer | Has on-peak hours | 0.20 |
| Winter | Has on-peak hours | 0.10 |
| Summer or winter | No on-peak hours (flat) | None |

## Hypothetical worked cases

Hypothetical input: the most recent export credit in the history is 27.40.

- Summer bill on a time-of-use schedule: 27.40 multiplied by 0.20, a holdback of 5.48.
- Winter bill on a time-of-use schedule: 27.40 multiplied by 0.10, a holdback of 2.74.
- Any bill on a flat schedule: no holdback.

title: Paired Battery Storage under Net Energy Metering Riders
content:
A battery may be paired with a Net Energy Metering system only under a rider that allows storage, and only up to that rider's storage capacity limit.

| Rider | Battery may be paired | Largest paired battery (kWh) | Grid-charged battery energy may be exported for credit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering | No | 0 | No |
| Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering | Yes | 40 | No |
| Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff | Yes | 40 | No |
| Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff | Yes | 200 | No |
| Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering | Yes | 1000 | No |
| Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff | Yes | 4000 | No |

## Points of the table

- The legacy rider shows a storage limit of 0 kWh because storage is not allowed under it.
- Under the five riders that allow storage, the paired battery capacity may equal the figure in the table; a larger battery is outside the rider's limit.
- No rider allows energy charged into the battery from the grid to be exported for credit.
- Hypothetical illustration: a 40 kWh battery is within the limit of Rider NEM-R and Rider NBT-R; a 45 kWh battery is within the limit of Rider NBT-C but not of the two residential riders.

title: Permission to Operate: Inspection, Approval Validity and Meter Requirements by Net Energy Metering Rider
content:
After approval, a Net Energy Metering system needs permission to operate before it exports under its rider. The rider sets whether a company witness inspection comes first, how long an approval stays valid, how quickly permission is issued, and whether a bidirectional meter must be in service.

| Rider | Witness inspection before permission to operate | Approval validity (months) | Business days to issue permission after a passed inspection, or after the installation notice where no inspection is required | Bidirectional meter in service before permission to operate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering | Not required | 12 | 5 | Required |
| Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering | Not required | 12 | 5 | Required |
| Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff | Not required | 12 | 5 | Required |
| Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff | Required | 12 | 10 | Required |
| Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering | Required | 18 | 10 | Required |
| Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff | Required | 24 | 15 | Required |

## Points of the table

- Under the three residential riders no witness inspection is required, and the 5 business days run from the installation notice.
- Under the three business riders the business days run from a passed inspection.
- A bidirectional meter must be in service at the address under every rider.
- Approval validity is 12 months except under Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering (18 months) and Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff (24 months).

title: Customer Care Academy — Net Energy Metering and Other Company Programs
content:
These answers state how Net Energy Metering interacts with the meter opt-out, demand response battery dispatch and budget billing, and with the loss of legacy grandfathering.

**Rules.** Holding a Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter excludes net metering until the customer returns to a communicating meter. A battery enrolled in a demand response battery dispatch program may export during demand response events, and that export earns the normal export credit; the demand response incentive is paid separately and never reduces or replaces the export credit. Budget billing on the service agreement does not change export credits; credits applied to a bill reduce the actual charges that budget billing compares with its installment. A legacy agreement that loses grandfathering moves to the rider open for new applications for the customer's class.

## Questions and answers

**A customer has a Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter and asks about net metering.**
Net metering is excluded while the opt-out meter is held; it becomes available once the customer has returned to a communicating meter.

**A battery enrolled in a demand response battery dispatch program discharges to the grid during an event. Does that export earn credit?**
Yes. It earns the normal export credit, and the demand response incentive is paid separately; the incentive never reduces or replaces the export credit.

**The customer is on budget billing. Are export credits smaller or larger because of the plan?**
Neither. Budget billing does not change export credits. The credit applied to a bill lowers the actual charges, and it is those reduced actual charges that budget billing compares with the installment.

**Where does a legacy agreement go when it loses grandfathering?**
To the rider open for new applications for the customer's class.

## Summary

| Holding alongside net metering | Effect on Net Energy Metering |
|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | Net metering excluded until return to a communicating meter |
| Demand response battery dispatch | Event exports earn the normal export credit; incentive paid separately |
| Budget billing | Export credits unchanged; applied credit reduces the actual charges compared with the installment |

title: Provisional Factor for Repeated Estimated Reads — Net Energy Metering Export Estimates
content:
A Net Energy Metering export estimate is reduced when the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system has had other bills issued on estimated closing reads in the past year.

**Rule.** When, besides the estimated period's own bill, two or more bills of the hosting service agreement dated in the 12 months before the booking were issued on an estimated closing read, the provisional factor is the repeated-estimate factor of 0.85. When exactly one such other bill was, it is the second-estimate factor of 0.92. When there is no such other bill, no provisional reduction applies.

The bills counted are the service bills of the hosting Electric Service Agreement whose bill dates fall in the 12 months before the booking and whose read type is estimated. The estimated period's own bill is one of them and is not counted toward the "other" bills.

## Provisional factor by count

| Estimated bills dated in the 12 months, including the estimated period's own bill | Other estimated bills | Provisional factor |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | No provisional reduction |
| 2 | 1 | 0.92 |
| 3 or more | 2 or more | 0.85 |

## Questions on the factor

**The estimated period's bill is the only estimated bill of the year. Is the estimate reduced?** No; there is no other estimated bill, so no provisional reduction applies.

**Two earlier bills of the year were estimated as well. Which factor applies?** Two other estimated bills reach the repeated-estimate count: 0.85.

**Hypothetical worked figure.** An estimate basis of 500 kWh with one other estimated bill in the year: 500 multiplied by 0.92 is 460 kWh, before any rounding at the end of the estimate.

title: Settlement Worksheet — Payout When a Net Energy Metering Agreement Is Ended at the Customer's Request
content:
This worksheet fixes the payout and the surrendered amount when a customer ends a Net Energy Metering agreement while keeping electric service at the address.

## Quantities

- **Bank**: the credit bank balance recorded on the agreement when the termination is recorded.
- **Early exit charge**: none. **Meter reconfiguration charge**: none.
- **Open-period holdback**: the export credit of the most recent billing period in the net metering history multiplied by the holdback share, rounded to the cent. The holdback share is nil, so the holdback is zero.
- **Paid share**: 1.

## The calculation

The requested-termination payout is the bank less the early exit charge, less the meter reconfiguration charge and less the open-period holdback, never below zero, multiplied by the paid share and rounded to the cent once. The surrendered amount is the bank less the requested-termination payout.

| Step | Quantity |
|---|---|
| 1 | Bank less the early exit charge, the meter reconfiguration charge and the open-period holdback |
| 2 | A negative result from step 1 is taken as zero |
| 3 | Step 2 multiplied by the paid share, rounded to the cent once: the payout |
| 4 | Bank less the payout: the surrendered amount |

## Hypothetical worked figure

Hypothetical inputs: a credit bank balance of 352.18 when the termination is recorded; the most recent export credit in the history is 27.40.

- Deductions: early exit charge 0.00, meter reconfiguration charge 0.00, and a holdback of 0.00, since the holdback share is nil.
- Payout: 352.18 multiplied by 1, that is 352.18.
- Surrendered amount: 0.00.

title: Valuation Worksheet — Revalued Export Credit Amount under Net Energy Metering
content:
This worksheet fixes the amount and the two per-kWh rates of a revalued export credit under the retail-valued Net Energy Metering riders (Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering, Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering and Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering).

## The calculation

1. **The credit revalued.** The export credit is the most recent export credit in the net metering history, that is, the one with the latest billing period end. Its on-peak and off-peak export kWh are taken as recorded on it, and their total is the recorded total export kWh.
2. **Export kWh by period of day.** Every exported kWh is valued as off-peak: the on-peak export kWh are zero and the off-peak export kWh are the recorded total.
3. **Seasonal energy rate.** Each revalued rate starts from the winter energy rate of the rate schedule of the service agreement hosting the system: the winter on-peak energy rate for the revalued on-peak rate, and the winter off-peak energy rate for the revalued off-peak rate.
4. **Supply-cost component and non-bypassable charge.** No supply-cost component is added and no non-bypassable charge is deducted.
5. **Revalued rates.** Each revalued rate is the seasonal energy rate, plus the supply-cost component, less the non-bypassable charge, rounded to five decimals.
6. **Revalued export credit.** The on-peak export kWh valued at the revalued on-peak rate, plus the off-peak export kWh valued at the revalued off-peak rate, the sum rounded to the cent once.

**Credit on an estimated read.** For an export credit whose billing period's service bill was issued on an estimated closing read, the revalued export credit is the amount already recorded on it.

## Rounding points

| Quantity | Rounded |
|---|---|
| Each revalued rate | To five decimals, after the energy rate, the supply-cost component and the non-bypassable charge are combined |
| Revalued export credit | Once, to the cent, on the sum of the two valued parts |

## Hypothetical worked figure

Hypothetical inputs: the most recent export credit records 140 kWh on-peak and 380 kWh off-peak; the hosting schedule's winter on-peak energy rate is 0.19000 and its winter off-peak energy rate 0.11000 USD per kWh; the bill for that period was issued on an actual read.

- Export kWh: on-peak 0, off-peak 520.
- Revalued on-peak rate: 0.19000. Revalued off-peak rate: 0.11000.
- Revalued export credit: 0 multiplied by 0.19000, plus 520 multiplied by 0.11000, that is 57.20.

title: Tariff Interpretation Note: Summer and Winter Energy Rates in Net Energy Metering Export Credit Revaluation
content:
When an export credit under a retail-valued Net Energy Metering rider (Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering, Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering or Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering) is revalued, each revalued rate starts from a seasonal energy rate of the rate schedule of the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system.

**Rule.** When the bill's season is summer and the schedule has on-peak hours, the revalued on-peak rate starts from the schedule's summer on-peak energy rate and the revalued off-peak rate from its summer off-peak energy rate. When the bill's season is summer and the schedule has no on-peak hours, both start from the schedule's summer off-peak energy rate, which is its single summer rate. Otherwise both start from the schedule's winter energy rates: the winter on-peak energy rate for the revalued on-peak rate and the winter off-peak energy rate for the revalued off-peak rate.

**Which bill and which schedule.** The season of the export credit is the pricing season printed on the service bill of the Electric Service Agreement whose billing period ends on the export credit's billing period end. The schedule is the rate schedule of the service agreement hosting the system. A schedule has on-peak hours when its on-peak hours are a clock window; a flat schedule has none.

## Energy rate selected

| Season on the bill | Schedule with on-peak hours (time-of-use) | Schedule without on-peak hours (flat) |
|---|---|---|
| Summer | On-peak rate: summer on-peak energy rate. Off-peak rate: summer off-peak energy rate | Both rates: the single summer energy rate |
| Winter | On-peak rate: winter on-peak energy rate. Off-peak rate: winter off-peak energy rate | Both rates: the winter energy rate of the schedule |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A credit whose matching service bill shows the summer season, on a time-of-use schedule with summer energy rates of 0.27000 on-peak and 0.11500 off-peak: the revalued rates start from 0.27000 and 0.11500.
- The same credit on a flat schedule whose single summer rate is 0.14000: both revalued rates start from 0.14000.
- A credit whose matching bill shows the winter season: both rates start from the schedule's winter on-peak and winter off-peak energy rates, whatever the schedule type.

title: Staying-Customer Uplift on Net Energy Metering Move-Out Payouts
content:
At a Net Energy Metering move-out termination, a staying uplift depends on whether the customer, having closed the service agreement hosting the system, holds other electric service with the company.

**Rule.** When the hosting service agreement is closed and the customer holds an Electric Service Agreement in active status, the staying uplift is the active-service uplift of 0.10. When the hosting service agreement is closed and the customer holds no service agreement in active status but holds one in pending start status, it is the pending-start uplift of 0.05. Otherwise no staying uplift applies.

**Records read.** The status of the hosting Electric Service Agreement, and the statuses of every Electric Service Agreement the customer holds.

## Uplift

| Hosting service agreement | Customer's other Electric Service Agreements | Staying uplift |
|---|---|---|
| Closed | At least one active | 0.10 |
| Closed | None active, at least one pending start | 0.05 |
| Closed | None active and none pending start | None |
| Not closed | Any | None |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- The customer closed the hosting agreement and already has an active agreement at a new address: 0.10.
- The customer closed the hosting agreement and the new address is still in pending start status: 0.05.
- The customer closed the hosting agreement and holds no other agreement: no staying uplift.

title: Regulatory Affairs Note — Power Supply Cost Recovery in Revalued Net Energy Metering Export Credits
content:
A revalued export rate under a retail-valued Net Energy Metering rider may include a supply-cost component drawn from the Power Supply Cost Recovery factor of the rate schedule of the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system.

**Rule.** Under the legacy rider's retail energy rate basis, the full Power Supply Cost Recovery rate of the schedule is added. Under the retail-rate-less-non-bypassable-charge basis on a residential rider, the Power Supply Cost Recovery rate multiplied by the successor supply share of 0.60, rounded to five decimals, is added. Otherwise, as for the aggregated business rider, nothing is added.

The component is added to both revalued rates, the on-peak and the off-peak alike.

## Component by rider

| Rider | Valuation basis and customer class | Supply-cost component added to each revalued rate |
|---|---|---|
| Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering | Retail energy rate; residential | The schedule's full Power Supply Cost Recovery rate |
| Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering | Retail energy rate less the non-bypassable charge; residential | The Power Supply Cost Recovery rate multiplied by 0.60, rounded to five decimals |
| Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering | Retail energy rate less the non-bypassable charge; business | Nothing |

## Hypothetical worked figures

Hypothetical input: a hosting schedule whose Power Supply Cost Recovery factor is 0.00421 USD per kWh.

- Under Rider NEM-L the component is 0.00421.
- Under Rider NEM-R it is 0.00421 multiplied by 0.60, that is 0.002526, rounded to 0.00253.
- Under Rider NEM-A it is zero.

title: Regulatory Note — Share of Surplus Credit Paid at a Net Energy Metering Move-Out
content:
At a Net Energy Metering move-out termination, the share of the surplus that is paid depends on the rider's valuation basis and on whether the agreement's recent export credits outran the credit applied to its bills.

**Rule.** Under the legacy rider's retail energy rate basis, when the export credits banked for billing periods ended in the 12 months before the termination exceed the credit applied to bills for those periods, the surplus share is the legacy surplus share of 0.75. Under the retail-rate-less-non-bypassable-charge basis, when those export credits exceed that applied credit, it is the successor surplus share of 0.55. In every other case no reduced surplus share applies.

**Records read.** From the net metering history: the amounts of the export credits and of the credit applications whose billing periods ended in the 12 months before the termination. From the rider: its valuation basis — the retail energy rate for Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering, the retail energy rate less the non-bypassable charge for Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering and Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering.

## Surplus share

| Valuation basis | Export credits of the 12 months compared with credit applied for those periods | Surplus share |
|---|---|---|
| Retail energy rate | Greater | 0.75 |
| Retail energy rate less the non-bypassable charge | Greater | 0.55 |
| Either retail basis | Equal or smaller | No reduced share |
| Avoided-cost export rate | Any | No reduced share |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- Rider NEM-R agreement with export credits of 640.00 and applied credit of 590.00 for the 12 months: the exports are greater, so 0.55.
- The same agreement with exports and applied credit both 590.00: not greater, so no reduced share.

title: Schedule of System Size Limits and Annual Usage Cap — Net Energy Metering
content:
Every Net Energy Metering rider limits the nameplate inverter capacity of the system, in kW AC, and caps the system's expected annual output against the annual usage of the address. The figures below are the rider values the size rule reads.

## Capacity limits and size cap

| Rider | Smallest system (kW AC) | Largest system (kW AC) | Size cap, as a fraction of annual usage | Expected annual output per kW AC (kWh per kW) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering | 0.5 | 20.0 | 1.10 (110 percent) | 1150 |
| Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering | 0.5 | 25.0 | 1.10 (110 percent) | 1150 |
| Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff | 0.5 | 25.0 | 1.50 (150 percent) | 1150 |
| Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff | 1.0 | 150.0 | 1.10 (110 percent) | 1150 |
| Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering | 10.0 | 1000.0 | 1.00 (100 percent) | 1150 |
| Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff | 150.0 | 2000.0 | 1.00 (100 percent) | 1150 |

## Annual usage used for the cap

| Rider | Look-back for annual usage | Address with fewer bills than the look-back |
|---|---|---|
| All six riders | The 12 most recent regular bills | The customer's stated annual load estimate |

The annual usage of the address is the total metered kWh of the 12 most recent regular bills of the service agreement before the application date. Where the address has fewer bills than that, the customer's stated annual load estimate is used instead.

## Reading the schedule

- Expected annual output is the nameplate capacity multiplied by 1150 kWh per kW under every rider.
- The size cap is the rider's fraction multiplied by the annual usage of the address. Under Rider NBT-R the cap fraction is 1.50; under Rider NEM-A and Rider NBT-L it is 1.00, so expected output may equal but not exceed annual usage.
- Hypothetical illustration: an address with 9200 kWh of annual usage under a rider whose cap fraction is 1.10 may host expected output of up to 10120 kWh, which is 1150 kWh per kW multiplied by 8.8 kW AC.

title: Net Energy Metering Rider Terms — Expiry Share by Years in Operation
content:
The share of unused carried Net Energy Metering credit that expires at the anniversary true-up falls as the agreement's time in operation grows.

**Rule.** When the whole calendar months from the permission to operate date to the expiry are at least the long-tenure months of 60, the expiry share is the long-tenure expiry share of 0.50. When they are at least the mid-tenure months of 24 but below 60, it is the mid-tenure expiry share of 0.75. Below 24 months no reduced expiry share applies.

The permission to operate date is the date recorded on the agreement; the expiry is the day the expiry is booked.

## Expiry share

| Whole calendar months from permission to operate to the expiry | Expiry share |
|---|---|
| 60 or more | 0.50 |
| 24 to 59 | 0.75 |
| Fewer than 24 | No reduced share |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- Permission to operate on 12 August; expiry booked on 11 August five years later: 59 whole months, so 0.75. Booked on 12 August five years later: 60 months, so 0.50.
- Expiry booked on 11 August two years after permission to operate: 23 months, no reduced share; on 12 August two years after, 24 months, so 0.75.

title: Tenure Months Added at a Net Energy Metering Move-Out Termination
content:
At a Net Energy Metering move-out termination, months are added to the full-value months for an agreement that has operated a long time.

**Rule.** When the whole calendar months from the permission to operate date to the termination are at least the long-tenure threshold of 48, the tenure months are the long-tenure bonus of 0.5. When they are at least the mid-tenure threshold of 24 but below 48, the tenure months are the mid-tenure bonus of 0.25. Below 24 months no tenure months are added.

The permission to operate date is the date recorded on the agreement; the termination is the day the termination is recorded.

## Tenure months

| Whole calendar months from permission to operate to the termination | Tenure months |
|---|---|
| 48 or more | 0.5 |
| 24 to 47 | 0.25 |
| Fewer than 24 | None |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- Permission to operate on 5 June; termination on 4 June four years later: 47 whole months, so 0.25.
- Termination on 5 June four years later: 48 whole months, so 0.5.
- Termination on 4 June two years later: 23 whole months, so none; on 5 June two years later, 24 months, so 0.25.

title: Net Billing Rider Terms — Share of the Bank Paid When the Customer Ends Net Energy Metering
content:
Under the Net Energy Metering riders valued at the avoided-cost export rates — Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff, Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff and Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff — only a share of the bank is paid when the customer ends the agreement while keeping service, and that share depends on enrollment in Demand Response Programs.

**Rule.** When the rider values exports at the avoided-cost export rates and the customer holds an active demand response enrollment, the paid share is the dispatch paid share of 0.95. When the rider values exports at the avoided-cost export rates and the customer holds no active demand response enrollment, it is the other paid share of 0.85. Under a retail-valued rider no reduced paid share applies.

**Records read.** The rider's valuation basis; the status of the customer's Demand Response Programs enrollments.

## Paid share

| Rider | Active Demand Response Programs enrollment | Paid share |
|---|---|---|
| Avoided-cost rider | Yes | 0.95 |
| Avoided-cost rider | No | 0.85 |
| Retail-valued rider (Rider NEM-L, Rider NEM-R) | Any | No reduced share |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A Rider NBT-R customer enrolled and active in a battery dispatch program: 0.95.
- A Rider NBT-R customer whose enrollment is only enrolled and not yet active: 0.85.
- A Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering customer: no reduced share.

title: On-Peak and Off-Peak Export kWh in Revalued Net Energy Metering Export Credits
content:
In the revaluation of an export credit under a retail-valued Net Energy Metering rider, the exported kWh of the credit are divided between on-peak and off-peak according to the rate schedule of the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system and the way the closing meter reading of its service bill was obtained.

**Rule.** When the schedule has on-peak hours and the bill's closing read is not a customer read, the on-peak and off-peak export kWh are taken as recorded on the export credit. When the schedule has on-peak hours and the closing read is a customer read, the on-peak export kWh are the recorded total export kWh multiplied by the customer-read on-peak share of 0.22, rounded to a whole kWh, and the off-peak export kWh are the rest of the total. Otherwise every exported kWh is off-peak.

The bill read is the service bill of the Electric Service Agreement whose billing period ends on the export credit's billing period end; its read type shows whether the closing read was an actual read, an estimated read or a customer read. The recorded total export kWh are the on-peak plus the off-peak export kWh recorded on the credit.

## Division of the export kWh

| Schedule | Closing read of the bill | On-peak export kWh | Off-peak export kWh |
|---|---|---|---|
| Has on-peak hours | Not a customer read | As recorded on the credit | As recorded on the credit |
| Has on-peak hours | Customer read | Recorded total multiplied by 0.22, rounded to a whole kWh | Recorded total less the on-peak export kWh |
| No on-peak hours (flat) | Any | Zero | The recorded total |

## Hypothetical worked cases

Hypothetical inputs: an export credit recording 96 kWh on-peak and 421 kWh off-peak, a recorded total of 517 kWh.

- Time-of-use schedule, bill issued on an actual read: 96 kWh on-peak and 421 kWh off-peak, as recorded.
- Time-of-use schedule, customer read: 517 multiplied by 0.22 is 113.74, so 114 kWh on-peak and 403 kWh off-peak.
- Flat schedule: 0 kWh on-peak and 517 kWh off-peak.

title: True-Up Period, Dispositions and Check Minimum — Net Energy Metering Rider Terms
content:
Under every Net Energy Metering rider the credit bank is settled once a year at the true-up and again when the agreement terminates. Each rider fixes the length of the true-up period, how the true-up month is set, the disposition of the bank at each anniversary true-up and at termination, and the smallest payout sent by check.

| Rider | True-up period (months) | True-up month | Anniversary true-up disposition | Termination disposition | Smallest payout sent by check (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering | 12 | Calendar month of the permission to operate date | Cash out | Cash out | 25.00 |
| Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering | 12 | Calendar month of the permission to operate date | Cash out | Cash out | 25.00 |
| Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff | 12 | Calendar month of the permission to operate date | Carry forward | Cash out | 25.00 |
| Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff | 12 | Calendar month of the permission to operate date | Cash out | Cash out | 100.00 |
| Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering | 12 | Calendar month of the permission to operate date | Forfeit | Forfeit | 100.00 |
| Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff | 12 | Calendar month of the permission to operate date | Cash out | Cash out | 100.00 |

## Points of the terms

- The three dispositions are cash out, carry forward and forfeit. Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff is the only carry-forward rider at the anniversary; Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering is the only rider that forfeits, at the anniversary and at termination alike.
- A payout that reaches the check minimum is paid by check; a smaller payout is credited to the service agreement. The minimum is 25.00 under the residential riders and 100.00 under the business riders.
- Hypothetical illustration: an agreement given permission to operate on 14 September has a September true-up month every year.

title: Settlement Desk Rules: Net Energy Metering True-Up and Termination Settlements
content:
These rules govern the settlement of the credit bank of a Net Energy Metering agreement at the annual true-up and at termination.

## Rules in force

1. **When the bank is settled.** At the bill dated in the true-up month, and when the agreement terminates, the residual bank is settled.
2. **Residual bank.** The residual bank at a settlement is the credit bank balance after every export credit and every credit application dated on or before the settlement date, including credit applied on bills dated that day.
3. **Method of payment.** A payout of at least the rider's check minimum is paid by check; a smaller payout is credited to the service agreement.
4. **Nothing to settle.** A residual of zero settles nothing.
5. **Once only, and only for these statuses.** Each settlement date and kind is settled once, and a settlement is booked only for an agreement in operating or terminated status.

The check minimum is the rider's figure in its true-up terms. Whether a settlement of the same date and kind already exists, and the agreement's status, are read from the company's records before a settlement is booked.

## Clauses no longer in force

The following clauses are no longer in force and have been superseded by the current settlement basis:

- the clause providing that at an anniversary true-up cash out pays the residual, carry forward leaves it in the bank, and forfeit zeroes it;
- the clause providing that at termination the residual is settled under the rider's termination disposition.

## Method of payment at the check minimum (hypothetical)

Hypothetical inputs: a rider whose check minimum is 25.00.

| Payout | Paid by |
|---|---|
| 24.99 | Credit to the service agreement |
| 25.00 | Check |
| 130.40 | Check |

## Status of the agreement

| Agreement status | Settlement may be booked |
|---|---|
| Operating | Yes |
| Terminated | Yes |
| Applied, approved, rejected, withdrawn or expired | No |

title: Final-Bill Desk Note: Vacancy Factor on Estimated Net Energy Metering Exports
content:
When the estimated period of a Net Energy Metering export credit ends in a final bill of the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system, a vacancy factor applies to the export estimate according to how far the final bill's usage has fallen.

**Rule.** When the estimated period's bill is a final bill and its billed kWh are below the low-use ratio of 0.50 multiplied by the billed kWh of the preceding period's bill, the vacancy factor is the empty-premises factor of 1.12. When it is a final bill and its billed kWh are at least that much, it is the partly-occupied factor of 1.05. On a regular bill no vacancy adjustment applies.

**Bills compared.** The estimated period's bill is the most recent service bill of the hosting Electric Service Agreement; its kind and its total billed kWh are printed on it. The preceding period's bill is the service bill whose billing period ends on the billing period end of the most recent export credit in the net metering history; its total billed kWh are compared.

## Vacancy factor

| Estimated period's bill | Billed kWh compared with 0.50 of the preceding bill's billed kWh | Vacancy factor |
|---|---|---|
| Final bill | Below | 1.12 |
| Final bill | Equal or above | 1.05 |
| Regular bill | Any | No vacancy adjustment |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

Hypothetical input: the preceding period's bill shows 800 kWh, so the comparison figure is 400 kWh.

- A final bill showing 399 kWh is below it: 1.12.
- A final bill showing exactly 400 kWh is not below it: 1.05.
- A regular bill showing 150 kWh: no vacancy adjustment.

title: Rate Department Table: Winter Retention Months at the Net Energy Metering Anniversary Cash-Out
content:
At the anniversary cash-out of a Net Energy Metering agreement, retention months are held in the bank when the winter bills of the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system make up a large part of the year's offsettable charges.

**Winter share.** The energy plus Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of the hosting service agreement's winter-season bills dated in the 12 months before the cash-out, divided by those charges of all its bills dated in those months, rounded to four decimals.

**Rule.** When the winter share is at least the high winter share of 0.60, there are the high retention months of 2. When it is at least the mid winter share of 0.40 but below 0.60, there is the mid retention month count of 1. Below 0.40 no retention months are held.

**Records read.** For each bill of the hosting Electric Service Agreement dated in the 12 months before the cash-out: its pricing season (summer or winter), its energy charge and its Power Supply Cost Recovery charge.

## Retention months

| Winter share | Retention months |
|---|---|
| 0.6000 or more | 2 |
| 0.4000 to 0.5999 | 1 |
| Below 0.4000 | None |

## Hypothetical worked cases

- Winter-season bills with energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of 712.40, out of 1180.00 for all bills of the 12 months: 712.40 divided by 1180.00 is 0.60373, rounded to 0.6037, so 2 retention months.
- Winter charges of 590.00 out of 1180.00: a share of 0.5000, so 1 retention month.
- Winter charges of 469.90 out of 1180.00: 0.39822, rounded to 0.3982, so none.
